The crash is fixed with a two-line change in `rich/text.py`, and both new tests pass. Against the original code, the inspect test fails with the same `IndexError` as the issue.

**Cause:** `Text.__init__` removes control characters (form feed `\x0c`, vertical tab `\x0b`, backspace `\x08`, carriage return `\r`) from the string it stores. But it set the text's length from the original string, before they were removed. When `inspect` builds a method's signature and docstring, it joins `Text` objects using that length. A docstring containing one of those characters therefore leaves style ranges pointing past the end of the text, and `Text.divide` crashes when it looks them up. pyparsing isn't installed in the venv, so I reproduced it with a hand-made docstring containing those characters rather than pyparsing itself.

**Fix** (`rich/text.py`, `Text.__init__`): measure the length from the cleaned-up string. `Text.append` already measured after stripping, so it didn't need a change.

The worker agent had also made `Text.divide` silently trim out-of-range style ranges. I removed that: it isn't needed once the length is right, and it would hide similar bugs in future.

**Tests added:**
- `tests/test_inspect.py::test_inspect_method_docstring_with_control_codes` inspects a class whose method docstring contains those characters, with `methods=True` and with `all=True, help=True`.
- `tests/test_text.py::test_control_codes_length` checks that the length, styles and line-splitting are correct after the characters are removed. On the original code it fails with `assert 7 == 4`.

**Test results:** the full suite gives 17 failed, 638 passed, 19 skipped. The worker agent found the same 17 failures on the unchanged code. I checked the three in `tests/test_inspect.py` myself (`test_inspect_text`, `test_inspect_builtin_function`, `test_inspect_integer_with_methods`): they fail identically without my change. They compare against the built-in docstrings of `str` and `int`, which differ in this Python version.

Nothing is committed.
